name: Question 11
problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $2$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=-4x$ defined on $[-1,1).$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of a series converging to the $2$-periodic extension of 

$$
G(x)=-2{x}^{2}={\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
-4x∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }{{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f$ is 
{{field-2}} 
on $R,$ we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term to get

$$
-2{x}^{2}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-3}}\cdot {{field-4}}.
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an odd function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=1$ and we are already given the coefficients ${b}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Now, notice that the function $F$ is continuous on $(-1,1).$ 
Therefore, the $2$-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{piecewise continuous}$ on $R,$ so we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}(-4t)\,\text{d}t & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi t)\,\text{d}t \\ [-2{t}^{2}]_{0}^{x} & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\cdot [-\frac{1}{n\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi t)]_{0}^{x} \\ -2{x}^{2} & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x))\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, notice that F(x) is an odd function. So, the Fourier series of its 2L-periodic extension has the form ∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nπxL).

In our case, L=1 and we are already given the coefficients bn for n≥1. Thus, the Fourier series of f(x) is given by f(x)∼∑n=1∞8(−1)nnπsin⁡(nπx).

Now, notice that the function F is continuous on (−1,1). Therefore, the 2-periodic extension f is piecewise continuous on R, so we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term:
